parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, facility ban or documented police targeting, and courts have intervened for gender recognition and detained foreigners. However politician-led hostility, rising anti-LGBT speech, pervasive reported discrimination/harassment highest for trans people, under-recorded hate crime with a pending amendment, and unresolved detention/prison placement with inconsistent lower-court practice create repeated visitor-facing exposure without reliably demonstrated correction.

entry_documents.protection: A regional court ordered re-issued certificates and diploma for a trans graduate in 2024.
entry_documents.interaction: No documented border rejection of foreign passports contrasts with domestic document correction; entry practice for nonbinary or mismatched markers remains unstated.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Prisons lack clear trans rules and are unprepared; immigration detention practice below supreme court is inconsistent.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: 2023 supreme administrative court requires vulnerability assessment before placement of detained trans foreigners.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A detained visitor reaches the supreme-court safeguard only after lower-level inconsistent handling; justice ministry resists binding prison regulation.

federal_state_facilities.protection: 2009 anti-discrimination law covers gender identity in access to goods and services.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No documented birth-sex bathroom or public-facility ban; service protection is statutory but no visitor enforcement outcomes are documented.

care_services.exposure: No visitor emergency-care or medication exposure documented.
care_services.interaction: Resident sexology and surgery gatekeeping does not establish visitor care practice; hospital ward placement is not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Head of state in 2021 called trans people disgusting; justice minister after 2024 ruling aimed to prevent men giving birth; far-right leaflets targeted LGBT activists.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Constitutional court in 2024 and regional human-rights court in 2025 rejected surgical/sterilisation conditions for legal gender recognition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Strong courts sit alongside highest-level political hostility, which the survey links to rising intolerance and 71% anti-LGBT political speech in 2023.

minors_guardians.interaction: Organised parental opt-outs from school LGBTI content concern resident schooling, not a documented travelling minor or guardian restriction.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: LGBTQ survey reported 43% discrimination/harassment and 51% insults, assault or threats over five years, highest among trans and non-binary respondents; hate-crime recording understates bias crime.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police recorded 94 hate crimes in 2024, with 46 prosecuted and 42 sentenced, including LGBTI-motivated incidents.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Some prosecution operates, but statistics do not reliably separate bias crimes, bias-factor amendment is pending, and vulnerable-victim status was weakened.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Prison regulation, statute for removal of surgery requirement, and hate-crime amendment remain unresolved or pending.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Anti-discrimination law and court interventions provide some recourse; 2026 commercial guide rates major cities more open, harassment rural and late-night, but this is not official data.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are strongest in constitutional litigation and weakest in detention/prison practice and everyday service correction, which are not documented as effective.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in pervasive discrimination and weak hate-crime recording, but this dossier documents 42 sentences and supreme-court detention safeguards, with no facility or custody mandate, so it sits above 0.45.

Closest: no trans offence or facility ban, recurring service and street hostility, slow or incomplete correction, and unmonitored custody; official hostility here is stronger, offset partly by court-ordered remedies.

Higher than this case because 0.65-A documents refunds, training and verified compliance after refusals and convictions, whereas here service correction and detention practice are not shown to operate reliably below top courts.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: courts provide real but mainly resident-facing and top-level protection, while everyday encounters are shaped by political hostility, reported discrimination and inconsistent detention handling. No universal facility exclusion or organised targeting is documented, preventing a lower score. Yet the absence of demonstrated service correction, pending hate-crime reform, undercounting and unresolved prison rules prevent the 0.65 reduced-risk tier. If detained, a visitor faces the clearest exposure: vulnerability assessment is required in principle but practice and placement remain unprepared and contested.
